PixelArtistry · Kimi Game Pipeline

Rebuild the setup from my video "I Created My Own Game with Kimi K3.1 Using Only Local 3D AI (Godot + Blender)": Kimi K3.1 Pro in Kimi Code controls ComfyUI, Blender and Godot through MCP, and every image and 3D asset is generated locally on Windows.

▶ The full story, with screenshots: https://pixel-artistry.com/blog/kimi-game-pipeline/ ▶ Full guide: https://pixelartistry.github.io/PixelArtistry-Kimi-Game-Pipeline/ ▶ Video: TODO: add the video link · PixelArtistry on YouTube

From concept to game

Concept 3D props First level Finished game

More work-in-progress and final screenshots are in the guide.

The pipeline

                 Kimi K3.1 Pro in Kimi Code  (reads my prompts, drives the apps through MCP)
                   │               │                 │                  │
                   ▼               ▼                 ▼                  ▼
  Concept images ──► Image to 3D ──────► Blender cleanup ──► Godot game
  Qwen Image 2.1     TRELLIS.2/Pixal3D   size, pivot,        level, gameplay,
  (ComfyUI)          + UltraTex (ComfyUI) collision, GLB      automated playtest

The only step I did by hand was rigging and animating the hero, in ActionForge.

Hardware

  • Windows 10/11, NVIDIA RTX GPU
  • 8 GB VRAM or more, 12 GB+ is comfortable. The 3D steps peaked at about 7–9 GB in my tests. I built the game on an RTX 5080 (16 GB).
  • 32 GB RAM recommended, plenty of free disk space for the models
  • A Kimi plan that includes K3.1 Pro

Quick start

[!IMPORTANT] No ComfyUI yet? Start with my TRELLIS.2 Installation Guide. It walks you through ComfyUI-Easy-Install and TRELLIS.2 step by step, and the workflows in this repo build on that setup.

  1. Install the Kimi Code CLI (PowerShell), log in, and pick K3.1 Pro with /model:
    irm https://code.kimi.com/kimi-code/install.ps1 | iex
kimi login
    K3.1 Pro Highspeed is faster but costs 2× the usage.
  2. Copy config/mcp.example.json to %USERPROFILE%\.kimi-code\mcp.json and replace the placeholder paths.
  3. Install the ComfyUI nodes and models: requirements.
  4. Copy the workflows into ComfyUI\user\default\workflows\Kimi\.
  5. Start ComfyUI, start Blender with the MCP add-on's server, run kimi, then type /mcp: comfyui, blender and godot should be connected.
  6. Work through the prompts in order.

Step-by-step instructions, troubleshooting and tips are on the guide site.

What Kimi changed in my workflow

Kimi started from my PixelArtistry_05p_Image_to_LowPoly_Prop_UltraTex workflow and tested one change at a time:

Setting My original Kimi's version
LODTailor high-poly cap 6,000,000 tris 50,000 tris
WTiVo final_res 1536 1024
Final low-poly target 2k tris 4k tris

The game project and the generated assets are not part of this repo; only screenshots are (docs/images).

Licences

The models have their own licences. The weights of Qwen Image 2.1 (Qwen Research License) and FLUX.2 [klein] base 9B, used by UltraTex (FLUX Non-Commercial License), are non-commercial, but the images and textures you generate can be used commercially: BFL's licence says so, and Qwen confirmed on X that outputs aren't part of the licensed materials. I'm not a lawyer, so read the licences yourself and make your own call before using the results commercially. Details are on the ComfyUI page.

Node packs by MostAadTech (GitHub · YouTube): WTiVo, LODTailor, Quad Reconstruct, Memory Cleaner and the UltraTex GGUF nodes. Please support him.
